body:
I traced this with some printf-debugging into third_party/grpc/bazel/generate_cc.bzl where a `ctx.actions.run` doesn't pass `use_default_shell_env = True,` as all functions from protobuf do.

Adding that fixes the issue.
Could you please send a PR?

issue.title: grpc protobuf compilations do not pass through PATH even if --client_env=PATH

labels.name: team-OSS
labels.description: Issues for the Bazel OSS team: installation, release processBazel packaging, website

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
### Description of the problem / feature request:

I am building Bazel on Windows at my company from scratch on a build server that does not have the MSVC runtime installed. Instead, we provide the path to the MSVC runtime dll directories in PATH. Bazel generally handles this pretty well (including other invocations of protoc.exe) but I found one action that doesn't. Using procmon I found the subprocess that doesn't receive PATH:

"C:\dev\cayman_bazel\build\temp\bazel_yDk0ywS3\out\execroot\io_bazel\bazel-out\host\bin\external\com_google_protobuf\protoc.exe" --plugin=protoc-gen-PLUGIN=bazel-out/host/bin/third_party/grpc/cpp_plugin.exe --PLUGIN_out=bazel-out/x64_windows-opt/bin --proto_path=. --proto_path=. --proto_path=bazel-out/x64_windows-opt/bin/external/com_google_protobuf/_virtual_imports/descriptor_proto --proto_path=bazel-out/x64_windows-opt/bin src/main/protobuf/command_server.proto

This appears to come from https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/bazel/generate_cc.bzl

### Feature requests: what underlying problem are you trying to solve with this feature?

I am trying to build Bazel from scratch without the MSVC runtime installed but with those dlls present in PATH and --client_env=PATH provided

### Bugs: what's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.

1. Make a copy of the MSVC 14 runtime dlls in a temp directory.
2. Either uninstall the MSVC 14 runtime or rename C:\windows\system32\vcruntime140.dll to C:\windows\system32\vcruntime140.dll.backup.
3. Build Bazel from scratch with VS2015/VS2017/VS2019 using the instructions https://docs.bazel.build/versions/master/install-compile-source.html

### What operating system are you running Bazel on?

Windows 10 x64 1909.

### What's the output of `bazel info release`?

I don't have bazel building yet, but I am building it from scratch using the 3.3.0 source.

### If `bazel info release` returns "development version" or "(@non-git)", tell us how you built Bazel.

Haven't built it yet.

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin ; git rev-parse master ; git rev-parse HEAD` ?

This outputs a bunch of stuff about our internal mirror and some patches we added on top. Our source commit is:

0f56df82bf Wed Jun 17 08:51:49 2020 noreply@google.com - Release 3.3.0 (2020-06-17)

###  Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

No.

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

Here is a file with procmon output about the protoc invocation:

[problematic_protoc.txt](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/files/4989088/problematic_protoc.txt)

Here is an example of another protoc invocation that is fine:

[correct_protoc.txt](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/files/4989096/correct_protoc.txt)

issue.title: Fix environment for protobuf compilation in grpc

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
Add use_default_shell_env = True to protoc invocation for grpc to mirror what the protobuf cc_proto_library & co are doing
Fixes a failure in invocing protoc when it is build in a non-default environment (e.g. with a custom LD_LIBRARY_PATH)

Fixes #11852, fixes #11855

This is a regression from 2.x to 3.0. Not sure what causes these issues but likely the upgrade of the used protobuf from 3.6 to 3.11

issue.title: Bazel build using generate_cc fails in custom environment

repository.name: grpc
repository.description: C++ based gRPC (C++, Python, Ruby, Objective-C, PHP, C#)

issue.body:
### What version of gRPC and what language are you using?

v1.31.0-pre2 (b54a5b338637f92bfcf4b0bc05e0f57a5fd8fadd)

### What operating system (Linux, Windows,...) and version?

Linux, RHEL 7.4


### What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g. python version or version of gcc)

GCC 8

### What did you do?

Build TensorFlow which uses this project in a custom environment (PATH and LD_LIBRARY_PATH set to installed GCC and its libs)

### What did you expect to see?

Build completes

### What did you see instead?

Build fails when running `protoc` through `generate_cc` with errors like `protoc: /lib64/libstdc++.so.6: version `GLIBCXX_3.4.20' not found` because it wrongly tries to use the system libstdc++.so instead if the one from LD_LIBRARY_PATH

### Anything else we should know about your project / environment?

This issue was first noticed in Bazel 3 itself which copied the `generate_cc` from this project: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/11855 and https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/11852 and then happened in TensorFlow 2.3.0 too which uses this project directly https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/issues/41857
